gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-puritan: Eight Bit Dragon strides across widely spaced letters, towering lowercase and all, with a faint stroke shift. Puritan follows in rounded, sans-serif forms, its oversized e and a counters staying open to the side.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-questrial: Questrial reads flat and modern, as if cut from stencil, with every stroke one width under a tall band of lowercase. Eight Bit Dragon's slightly heavier thick lines make that sameness feel deliberate.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-radio-can: Widely separated letters and a towering lowercase give Eight Bit Dragon its loping, adventurous stride. Radio Canada then holds a steady, pressure-free line, its curves finishing in clear openings that keep a long page easy going.

Radio Canada Big is a plain sans with a tall x-height. Eight Bit Dragon sprawls above it in widely spaced, adventurous letters, while the body keeps one stroke width running through every line beneath.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-readex-pr: Loose-limbed and swaggering, Eight Bit Dragon spaces its towering lowercase wide, with strokes sitting between monoline and sharp contrast. Readex Pro runs a plain sans line below, unvarying from word to word.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-ruda: Eight Bit Dragon takes a relaxed stride in widely spaced letters, its strokes tapering gently like a sharpened carpenter's pencil. Ruda sits below as a wire-thin plain sans, wide-mouthed in its rounds and generous in x-height.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-saira: Saira keeps each s open enough to see through. Its rounded letters stretch toward the top line, and Eight Bit Dragon's gentle modulation and wide stride give the pair a bold yet unsnagged look.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-sarpanch: Big, swaggering and widely spaced, Eight Bit Dragon has towering lowercase and a moderate thick-thin shift. Sarpanch, a plain sans with an open-mouthed e and compact ascender gaps, quietly holds up the text below it.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-schibsted: Wide-striding and towering, with a gentle taper at every joint. Schibsted Grotesk, a plain sans with tall-bowled e and a, and terminals that never close in, is what keeps Eight Bit Dragon's adventurous swagger approachable.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-sen: Adventurous letters stride wide, their bowls faintly pen-like. Eight Bit Dragon brings that bold, towering personality, while Sen draws tall, constant-weight sans-serif lowercase with curves that end before turning inward.
